extracted.intended_audience: patent searchers and information specialists using the Questel.Orbit system (IP professionals, librarians, patent analysts)
extracted.subtask_description: Operational guidance for searching, manipulating, exporting and alerting on patent data in the Questel.Orbit system (commands, limits, display/print/SDI configuration and statistical analysis).

rubrics_metrics.name: MPUB merged record creation
rubrics_metrics.description: To create a merged record based on a set of documents use the MPUB command with a set of results. Use the HIS command to determine the SS number. Note: There is a limit of 1000 results per SS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When searching with assignee/inventor names, keywords or classes results may contain more than one record per invention; MPUB merges them. To display MPUB records: MPS displays the SDTR format plus the CT field; MPMX displays the MAX format minus the IDT, BC and UP fields. Example commands: PRT MPS, PRT MPMX.

rubrics_metrics.name: CITF forward citation search
rubrics_metrics.description: CITF runs a forward citation search on a set of records to retrieve patents that cite the patents in your initial set. The new result set contains both the original patents and the citing patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commands available in EPPATENT, FRPATENT, WOPATENT, USPAT, DEPAT & PLUSPAT. Use with a set of results; use HIS to determine SS number. Maximum initial set size for CITF is 1000 results per SS. Example: CITF SS 1. Can be used with FROM parameter in Cluster mode (e.g., CITF SS 1 FROM EPPATENT).

rubrics_metrics.name: CITB backward citation search
rubrics_metrics.description: CITB runs a backward citation search on a set of records to retrieve patents cited by the patents in your initial set. The new set contains both the original patents and the cited patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use with a set of results and HIS to determine SS number. Maximum initial set size for CITB is 1000 results per SS. Example: CITB SS 1. In Cluster mode use FROM parameter to limit database.

rubrics_metrics.name: FAMCITE family citation report
rubrics_metrics.description: FAMCITE creates a citation report for a patent family (available in the PlusPat file).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After conducting a family search for a single family, FAMCITE displays a complete citation report in three parts: original source family; citing patent families; cited patent families. Add IMG parameter to display clipped images. Examples: FAMCITE, FAMCITE IMG.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offline email delivery defaults and formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Default: documents resulting from the last search statement in MAX format (limited to 500 documents per order) and in ASCII format. An Internet address must be stored on your ID before using the email print option.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can receive documents in RTF, XML or PDF (with accents and special characters); files are UUencoded. To receive images include RTF and IMG parameters. Documents are sent within one hour of order. Example commands: PR EMAIL XML, TYPE XML PDF, SET EMAIL, PR EMAIL RTF IMG.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offline prints by mail defaults and ordering options
rubrics_metrics.description: Default: all records to a maximum of 5000 from the last search statement in Max format mailed to the stored permanent postal address (AD). Each offline print order is assigned a reference number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Options: choose specific fields, system or user-defined formats, ranges of records, page layouts, include images, combine parameters. In single DB environment default is current DB; in cluster default is all DBs in cluster order. Must set stored address with AD command before ordering. Alternate mailing address input methods described. Cancel offline print using order reference number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevancy ranking (RK command) and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Display search results in order of relevance (descending order of occurrence of search terms). Search results are stored in search statement 203 for display purposes. The RK command works with a maximum of 5000 records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may rank results from a specific search statement; when ranking from a previously selected database in a cluster use the FROM parameter. Examples: RK, RK SS 5, RK SS 2 FROM DWPI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online sorting behavior and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Sorted records are placed in SS 203 for display/printing/offline or crossfile searching (MEM). Sorted records cannot be used for further direct searching. Default: all records (up to ~5000).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can sort by a specific field, by a specific search statement, by specific result ranges, or by subfield/position (e.g., PRG 1, RK 4). Default position is 1st term; numeric data default is 1st subfield; default sort lengths: text=20, dates=10, numeric=16. Default direction ascending for text (+), descending for dates/numeric (-). Sort on up to 3 fields simultaneously (max total sort key length 100 characters). Use FROM when sorting from a previously selected database in a cluster. Example commands: SORT /IN, SORT SS 3 /IN, SORT 1-50 /PAN, SORT /PAN RK 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: User-defined display formats
rubrics_metrics.description: You can list pre-defined and user-defined formats, create user-defined formats, display records in user-defined formats and delete formats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: User format: up to 10 fields per user format; each format name up to 4 characters. User-defined formats can be saved per ID and are independent of database. Example: FOR PAT1 AN TI PA AB; PRT PAT1 1-2 SS 3; ER FOR PAT1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page layout (PSET) options and defaults
rubrics_metrics.description: User-defined page layouts set via PSET: several options including number (required, choose 1-30), margins, indentation, title, fixed/variable field lengths, blank lines between documents (default 1) and between fields (default 0), empty field display options.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defaults: left margin 0, right margin 0, indentation default 6 chars (max 20). Empty fields are not displayed by default; can be displayed as characters. Use LMG, RMG, LMC, FLDN, FLDT, DOC NPG, FLDE, etc. Example PSET NUMB 2 FLDT 18"-" LMC 20; PRT PSET.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memory lists (MEM) and cross-file extraction
rubrics_metrics.description: Four system-named memory lists: MEM1–MEM4; up to 150 user-named memory lists. Use qualifiers XPN for patent/publication numbers, XPR for priority numbers, XAP for application numbers and XCT for citation numbers. Maximum number of terms = 100,000 per memory list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MEM extracts every term from specified field from all records in the last search statement with results by default. Options: extract from specific search statement, range of records, previously selected database, to a named list. Named lists automatically saved for 7 days. Terms are appended (not overwritten) on each MEM command. Example: MEM /XPN, MEM SS 1 /XPN, MEM MYLIST /XPR, MEM IPG NODUPS /XPN.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extraction granularity and selection for MEM
rubrics_metrics.description: Extraction can target parts of a field: every term from a paragraph, specific sentence, every nth term, last item (PRG, SEN, RK). Extraction can include/exclude specific characters (max 4) and extract portions of a term to specific length/up to a character/embedded substring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extraction possible from up to 4 fields simultaneously. Combine parameters for complex extraction (examples: MEM /XPN PRG*, MEM /XPR WITH "US "). Example commands: MEM MEM3 200-300 /XPN WITH "FR" FROM INPD, MEM MYLIST STORE /XPN.

rubrics_metrics.name: Managing MEM lists (display/delete/keep/store)
rubrics_metrics.description: Display MEM lists (first 15 terms then next, continuous display, named lists, listing of all MEM lists). Delete terms (all, ranges, specified terms, terms including/excluding characters). Keep terms (specified terms or by character filters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Named lists saved 7 days by default; STORE a named MEM list to permanently save it (charged). Examples: PRT MEM, ER MEM, ER MEM 1-10, KEEP MEM 1-10, KEEP MEM WITH "EP", MEM MYLIST STORE /XPN.

rubrics_metrics.name: Searching with MEM lists and *MEM super-terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Search terms on a MEM list (default MEM1): in Basic Index, in specified fields, from a named list, with/without display. Use *MEM (or *MEM <name>) as a super-term combined with other search terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Super-terms allow reuse of MEM sets as part of larger searches. Examples: *MEM, *MEM /XPN, *MEM MYLIST /XPR, *MEM 1-10 /XPN AND HOECHST/PA.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEL command for MEM term searching
rubrics_metrics.description: SEL creates a search set from extracted and searched MEM terms and displays all terms with 0 or multiple postings when AUDIT is on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use SEL MEM1 /XPN to search all terms in MEM1 list. SEL is useful to build search sets from list-extracted terms and to audit term coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: MEMS statistical ranking (MEMSORT) command
rubrics_metrics.description: MEMS extracts, sorts and stores terms in default MEM2 for statistical analysis. MEMS defaults to a subset of 50 records from the last search; terms are ranked by descending frequency. Each MEMS overwrites the previous MEMS list; named lists allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Options: source (search statement, range, entire set, previously selected DB), limit display to values with occurrences > n or top n by frequency, rank alphabetically or numerically. Examples: MEMS SS 3 /DS, MEMS GT 20 /PA, MEMS TOP 10 /PA, MEMS ALPHA /INN. Named lists auto-saved for 7 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Searching from MEMS lists and *MEMS super-terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Search terms from a MEMS list (default MEM2) in Basic Index or specified fields, by specific term ranges or named lists. Use *MEMS as a super-term in search statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: *MEMS /PA, *MEMS 1-5 /INN, *MEMS SOAP /PAN. Super-term search statements limited to 2000 characters (approx 150 search terms). Use HEAT+/S and truncation operators in combination with MEMS as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: GET macro for quick statistical analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: GET <fieldlabel> (e.g., GET PA or GET /PA) runs a statistical analysis on the specified field and stores/sorts terms (alternative to MEMS for listed fields).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fields supported include Assignee, Inventor, Publication Country, Priority Country, Application Country, Publication Date, Priority Date, Application Date, IPC, Main IPC, European Classification, US Classification, Company Code. Use GET CC, GET IN, GET IPC, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporary saved searches (A SAVEd search)
rubrics_metrics.description: Search statements are automatically retained during a session and for 2 hours after logoff; reconnecting can restore them. A search can be saved temporarily for 7 days free of charge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can re-execute searches or specified statements. Commands: SAVE <name>, EX <name>, SHO <name>. Example: SAVE DIGITAL; EX DIGITAL; SHO DIGITAL. When changing databases statements are retained from previous file searched.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permanently stored searches (STORE) naming rules and management
rubrics_metrics.description: STORE creates a permanently saved search: enter a name max 8 characters including at least one letter; avoid special characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stored searches can be listed, displayed, executed (EX), partially executed (EX name 3 5-8), deleted (PURGE). Commands may be stacked with ; (e.g., EX REP1;EX REP2). In cluster environment use FROM parameter where required. Example: STORE REP1; SHO REP1; PURGE REP1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creating and managing SDIs (Saved Searches / Alerts)
rubrics_metrics.description: SDI is a saved search that runs at a predefined frequency and delivers results in MAX format (or other formats); SDIs can be defined across files and delivered by mail or email.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Easy Mode step-by-step: select DB & create strategy; enter SDI name & follow prompts; set Survey Fields (update codes) to determine delivery frequency/data searched; run SDI in up to 40 DBs; add up to 6 email addresses; select output type (TXT/RTF/PDF/XML), display format (default MAX), include drawings, choose page style, sort results up to 3 fields, assign subaccount. Example commands: SDI, FI PLUSPAT /PA CISCO SDI, Profile Name? SCAN1. See QWEB - SDI Assistant and Top Menu Bar Help & Services - Alerts.

rubrics_metrics.name: SDI email delivery and format constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: SDI results can be sent by Internet email in formats RTF, XML or PDF (TXT will not support images). To receive images include RTF or XML with PR IMG parameter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First set an Internet address with SET EMAIL. Examples: SDI SCAN1 EMAIL, SDI SCAN1 EMAIL RTF;SDI SCAN1 EMAIL RTF;PR IMG; SDI SCAN1 EMAIL XML;PR IMG. Use SET EMAIL before sending to ensure an address is stored on the ID.

rubrics_metrics.name: SDI modification (easy menu and expert commands)
rubrics_metrics.description: SDIs can be modified via menu prompts (Easy SDI Modification) or via precision commands (Expert SDI Modification).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Menu lets you change profile name, add/delete files, change survey fields, delivery type, email addresses, file format, display/print command, SDI title, page style, sort commands, subaccount. Expert mode: use 'shosdi ' to view, then 'set sdi ; ' to change single parameters (e.g., set sdi ; pr ). SDI modifications are billed at parking file rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Display and delivery formats (PDF/RTF/TXT/XML) and page styles
rubrics_metrics.description: Delivery formats: PDF (text+images; good for Acrobat), RTF (edit with MS Word; text+images), TXT (text only), XML (flexible, text+images). Page styles: Pg.Style 1-5 with different field/name and page-break combinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose format based on downstream use (PDF for print, RTF for editing, XML for structured output). Page Style examples: 1 Full Field Names w/o page breaks; 2 Full Field Names with page breaks; 3 Field tags w/o page breaks; 4 Field tags with page breaks; 5 Report format (Pluspat & Appalert). Use PR IMG to include images. Examples: set sdi ciscoplus ; pr mini img legal; set sdi ciscoplus email xml.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ordering documents (PDS Patent Delivery System) and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Use PDS/ORDER/EXPO/OR commands to order patent documents. You may order up to ten (10) PNs per order. Ordered documents by email return a ZIP and PDFs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Display PN with PRT XPN or LI XPN before ordering. Example commands: ORDER EXPO XPN WO200012362,EP-12345; OR EPO XPN WO200012362, EP--12345; SET EMAIL. Alternate addresses are prompted and cannot be stored for alternate addresses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permanent user options and display preferences (POP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Permanent user options: accented characters display (on/off), number of lines displayed per screen (min 10 default 24), characters per line (64–132 default 80), system language (French default, English available), truncation/display of generated terms, processing message frequency, highlighting options, image format and reduction, merged family display preference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commands: POP NL, POP NC, POP LA, POP TRUN SEL/AUTO/NONSTOP, POP AUDIT ON, POP HLIG ON TERM n/OFF, POP TLIM n, POP IMG GIF/TIFF, POP MFAM EP. Example: POP NL 50 NC 80 TRUN AUTO; POP IMG TIFF R25.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporary user options (OP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Modify options for the current session only via OP command (temporary, not persisted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: OP HLIG ON TERM 2. Use OP to test or temporarily change behavior without altering permanent POP settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of FROM parameter in Cluster environments
rubrics_metrics.description: The FROM parameter is essential in a Cluster environment with certain commands and optional with others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FROM is essential when using: JOIN, MEMS, RK, SO, SAVE, STORE, SDI, OR (ordering documents), UP. FROM is optional with: BR, FLD, FO, FOR, HIS, PRT, MEM. Always include FROM when instructed for correct cross-database operation in clusters.

rubrics_metrics.name: JOIN and *MDARC linking to structure databases
rubrics_metrics.description: JOIN transfers chemical compound numbers from selected bibliographic records to chemical structure files (and *MDARC transfers numbers reverse). Default: all compound numbers in last search (max 5,000 compounds; raised to 50,000 for MPHARM).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify target structure DB (WPAM or MPHARM) on MARKUSH DARC and name the saved list. Options to restrict to specific compounds or generic compounds (role N,T). Example: JOIN TO WPAM VIA LIST3 SPE; *MDARC NAME1. Graphical terminal emulation needed to display structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reserved terms and avoidance techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: Many Questel.Orbit commands/terms are reserved (e.g., IMAGE, ID, PRINT, FILE). System and proximity operators (W, D, F, S, P, L) are also reserved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three ways to retrieve reserved terms as search terms: 1) truncation, 2) place reserved term second (word order), 3) quotes to retrieve exact reserved term ("IMAGE"). Examples: IMAGE ? OR WATERMARK; "IMAGE" OR WATERMARK; /PA "S" W "F" W "D" LABS for 'S F D Labs'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stopwords in certain files and handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Some files (DWPI, IFIPAT, PHARM, CAS) have stopwords associated with chemical symbols; these are treated as stopwords only if they begin with a lower-case letter (e.g., a, at, be, he, in, and no).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To search the phrase 'in vitro' in stopword-free files use quotes: "IN" W VITRO. For DWPI/IFIPAT/PHARM/CAS drop the word 'in' from the request (use VITRO W FERTILI+).

rubrics_metrics.name: System limits (searches, memory lists, records, truncation, printing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Key system limits: 200 search statements per database; 2,030 characters per search statement; number of terms per memory list 100,000; terms per answer set using truncation 30,000; types of truncation per term 3; number of truncation symbols 7; default memory lists 4; up to 150 user-named MEM lists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other limits: Patent Grouping & ID command max 5,000 documents; SORT max 5,000 documents; RK max 5,000 documents; Family searches on a Search Set (FAM SS) max 1,000 records; proximity connector max words = 9 (e.g., transgenic 9d animal? valid; 10d will not process); Offline prints maximum: 5,000 by postal mail, 500 by email.
